clue.text: Go or stay with the team?

definitions.meaning: to go is to quit or leave a post
to sign a new contract and remain with the club

explanation.definitionFit: To quit a job is to give it up formally; read with a hyphen it means renewing a contract with a club.

clue.text: The nitty-gritty of conflict over team changes

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the word for conflict is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: conflict means war

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of team are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is getting down to the basics of a dispute over a reshuffled side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns WAR into RAW; 'changes' shuffles TEAM into MEAT. The phrase is also the theme: several of the other answers are steak dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw meat is used figuratively for the basic, unvarnished substance of something, the essential stuff.

clue.text: 1 down, seasoned wood two sailors brought into Kent

indicators.note: brought into says the wood and sailors are placed inside the letters for Kent

parts.note: Kent is in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
teak is a hardwood
a tar is a sailor; two of them give two copies
a tar is a sailor; two of them give two copies

explanation.surface: Some well-aged timber and a couple of seamen are shipped into a county in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seasoned' looks like it describes the wood but belongs to the definition: raw meat with seasoning. 'brought into' puts the wood and sailors inside the county's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak tartare is a dish of raw minced beef seasoned with capers, onion and spices, so it is seasoned raw meat.

clue.text: Fifty outrageous soldiers gathering around entrance for a breather

indicators.note: gathering around says the soldiers' letters enclose the other pieces

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
OTT, over the top, means outrageous

explanation.surface: Fifty wild troops gather around a doorway to take a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a breather' looks like a pause; it is anyone who breathes, and the glottis is the opening their air passes through.
explanation.definitionFit: The glottis is the opening between the vocal cords in the larynx, the way in for inhaled air.

clue.text: See 23
Michael Fish's go-between?

parts.note: Michael Fish was a well-known BBC weather forecaster; the item he showed between highs and lows on his weather maps was a line joining equal pressures

explanation.surface: What intermediary did the TV weatherman use?
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Fish was a long-serving BBC weather presenter. 'go-between' suggests a messenger, but it means a line drawn between pressure systems on a weather chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather map line connecting points of equal atmospheric pressure, drawn between highs and lows by forecasters.

clue.text: She tends to one man's rude offspring

definitions.text: She tends to one man's rude offspring

indicators.note: offspring are what is produced from parents, so the preceding letters breed something new by rearrangement

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
man's gives the letters MANS, the S included

explanation.surface: A woman looks after the bad-mannered children of a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offspring' signals the anagram, the letters breeding a new word. The whole clue also describes the answer: a woman who looks after someone's children.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to care for young children, tending offspring of the household.

clue.text: Bat the eyes? I can't possibly! I'm out of time!

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of I can't could be rearranged

parts.note: can't gives the letters CANT

indicators.note: out of says the letters of I'm are taken away from time

parts.note: the letters I and M as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests they cannot wink because they have run out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles ICANT into NICTA; 'out of' removes IM from TIME, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nictate is to blink, and to bat the eyes is to blink or flutter the eyelids.

clue.text: 2 from two of the cups that cheer up half braindead characters

parts.words: two of the cups that cheer
parts.note: the cups that cheer is a literary phrase for tea; cha is a slang word for tea

parts.words: two of the cups that cheer
parts.note: tea is the drink of the cups that cheer
U is the abbreviation for up

indicators.note: characters signals that the letters are treated as loose characters to be rearranged
half says only the first half of braindead is used

explanation.surface: Two cups of tea perk up someone who is half asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cups that cheer' (from Cowper) is tea, and CHA is tea too. 'half' takes the front of BRAINDEAD, BRAIND (the half is generous), and 'characters' rearranges it into BRIAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Chateaubriand is a thick cut of beef fillet, one of the steak dishes in this puzzle's theme.

clue.text: Precious little time ahead

indicators.note: ahead places the letter for time in front of the word for little

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: There is very little time left before an important moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious' looks like an adjective for the time; it is the definition, meaning affected.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious here means affectedly refined or overly dainty, the same sense as twee.

clue.text: Power of the great unwashed? Hooray! Left three hundred laundered

indicators.note: laundered, washed and churned, signals the letters are mixed up

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so three hundred is CCC

explanation.surface: Someone cheers mob rule, then mentions three hundred clean items left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laundered' plays against 'the great unwashed' while signalling the anagram of HOORAY with L and CCC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochlocracy is mob rule, government by the common rabble, here called the great unwashed.

clue.text: Henry II had no time for him, or for the Environment Secretary!

indicators.note: no time means the letter for time is taken away

parts.note: Margaret Beckett was the UK Environment Secretary when the puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A medieval king despised an archbishop, and a modern minister fares no better.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Becket was the archbishop Henry II quarrelled with and whose murder followed; 'had no time for him' is both the history and the instruction to drop a T from BECKETT.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands for the man Henry II could not abide, Archbishop Thomas Becket.

clue.text: The deficit say between Dixieland and a piano

indicators.note: between puts the word for say in the gap separating Dixieland from a piano

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz, of which Dixieland is a style
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A shortfall falls somewhere between a jazz band and a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade gap is a deficit in the balance of trade, imports exceeding exports.

clue.text: Top politico? Says he!

parts.note: states means says
a man is a he

explanation.surface: A leading politician makes a self-important claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesman is a senior, respected political leader.

clue.text: Rossini's 2 duets or no other

indicators.note: other signals the letters of duets or no are made into something else

explanation.surface: An opera composer writes duets, or nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: Rossini suggests the composer's music, but tournedos Rossini is a steak dish named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournedos Rossini is a classic dish of beef fillet topped with foie gras, named after the composer.

clue.text: How do you like your 2, almost 1 down?

definitions.meaning: the waiter's question about how a steak is cooked: lightly
lightly cooked meat is close to uncooked

explanation.definitionFit: Underdone steak, browned outside and red within, is nearly uncooked flesh.

clue.text: 15 down

definitions.meaning: an extreme of the previous answer: steak cooked even less

explanation.definitionFit: A very underdone steak is called blue, and feeling depressed is also feeling blue.

clue.text: Arabian revolutionary, hot for a new kingdom

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning things round, so the letters are rearranged
hot for a means the letter for hot replaces an A

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: An Arab rebel with a fiery temper founds a fresh realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps one A of ARABIAN for H, and 'revolutionary' rearranges the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Bahrain proclaimed itself a kingdom in 2002, so it was a recent monarchy when the puzzle appeared.

clue.text: Sailor's primitive shanty? Utter nonsense!

indicators.note: utter means speak out, so the phrase before it is to be heard spoken

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, ur- is a prefix for primitive, and a shanty is a ditty: AB'S UR-DITTY

explanation.surface: A seaman's crude old song is a load of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an intensifier for 'nonsense', but it signals speech: AB'S UR-DITTY, spoken, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An absurdity is something utterly ridiculous, nonsense in its fullest form.

clue.text: Countermand Kofi's diktat?

parts.note: Kofi Annan was Secretary-General of the UN
a diktat is an order

explanation.surface: Should one overrule a decree from the head of the United Nations?
explanation.definitionFit: To countermand is to cancel a command, which is what reversing an instruction does.

clue.text: See 2
Servitude when the majority take everything

indicators.note: the majority means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: R, for recipe, is Latin for take
everything means all

explanation.surface: Majority rule means the many grab the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrall is bondage or servitude, the state of being enslaved.

clue.text: Impress sailors' leader; suspend from yardarm, say

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of sailors'
say signals that the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to suspend from the yardarm is to hang high, the old naval punishment

explanation.surface: A navy captain coerces men and threatens to string up the ringleader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impress' means to force into naval service, the press gang's job.
explanation.definitionFit: To shanghai is to press-gang or force someone into service, which is what impressing seamen meant.

clue.text: Inspired to get one out of the wood

indicators.note: one out of the wood means the letters of one sit outside the wood

parts.note: fir is a wood

explanation.surface: Someone is told to come out of the forest to find inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' usually means taken from; here ONE lies outside FIR. 'Out of the wood' also suggests escaping trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on fire is to be performing brilliantly, inspired and full of energy.

clue.text: 2 prepared to bring GM food initially into line

indicators.note: prepared, as food is made ready, signals the letters are reworked
initially takes the first letter of food

explanation.surface: Steak is prepared after genetically modified food is brought into line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring' is a link; the anagram uses GM, F and INTO LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Filet mignon is a tender cut of beef from the narrow end of the fillet, served as steak.

clue.text: Could be hand-reared by the sweat of one's brow

definitions.text: by the sweat of one's brow

indicators.note: could be says the letters of hand-reared could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: An animal raised by hand was the result of much effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard-earned is gained only through toil, as by the sweat of the brow.

clue.text: Incline towards such 1 down and 2?

definitions.meaning: to incline towards is to tilt or be inclined to
meat or a steak without fat

explanation.definitionFit: To tilt towards something, and also meat free of fat, as good steak can be.

clue.text: Do their products make strong babies curl up?

definitions.text: Do their products make strong babies
definitions.meaning: a Swiss food company famous for baby milk formula
to curl up snugly or snuggle

explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss firm made baby formula, and the verb means to snuggle cosily.

clue.text: King with jester around: he will do contortions

indicators.note: around says the jester's letters are placed round the king's

parts.note: a wit is a joker or jester
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch with his fool will perform twisting tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm, making contortions with the body.
